missionPremise: The Smart Files design (`_design/smart-files/`, RATIFIED 2026-09-17, drawn against smart-files main 61c84f61) is not a file browser and refuses that vocabulary. Four things it requires, quoted from the dispatch as the acceptance sheet: five-key provenance REFUSES an incomplete write and never defaults a key; a new version is a REVISION of the same document, not a second file beside it; no file-browser vocabulary where the design forbids it, checked as a file not by eye; and `node _design/smart-files/check.mjs` passes with a NON-ZERO matched-input count, verified against a planted violation in both directions. The governing stance is COVERAGE BEFORE RESULTS. Source: `_dispatches/2026-09-18_g155-smart-files-build_dispatch.md` lines 96-116.
completionPredicate: Done means: (1) each of the four acceptance items is verified by VIOLATING it against real HTTP routes on real bytes, in both directions, with the output on record; (2) the design's own instrument passes with a non-zero matched-input count and is observed catching four planted violations; (3) the merged commit is serving production, read by JSON field name, and a probe proves the SERVING revision is the new code rather than a 200 that could have come from the old one; (4) the deployed QA surface carries the design's vocabulary, measured on the served bytes BEFORE and AFTER the deploy so the change is a paired control, not a claim.

No version of this lane's work was observed under load: the probes are correctness probes, and the coverage query adds a subquery per row plus a second aggregate query per listing. On the demo tenant (26 documents, 29 versions) that is invisible; on a city with tens of thousands of rows it is an unmeasured cost. Named rather than assumed away.

LESSON: A reason computed and returned in an HTTP response is not a recorded reason. If a fact matters after the response is gone, it needs a column with a constraint, and the read path needs an explicit state for rows written before that column existed ('reason-not-recorded') that is NEVER inferred from an adjacent field. The temptation to infer is strongest exactly where it is most damaging: inferring 'no-text-layer' from a PDF content type would have relabelled a corrupt PDF as a scan, and 29 production rows would have received invented reasons.

Your own diff can be honest and the DEPLOYED bytes still be wrong: the repo said Searchable/Placed against/Provenance, the live bundle said 'browse' twice and none of them. A file-level vocabulary check and a served-bytes check are two different instruments, and the served one is the only one that can see a stale deploy. Pair them, and run the served one BEFORE and AFTER the deploy so the change is a control rather than a claim.

A refusal rendered behind a closed dialog is a refusal that discards the user's work. If the product's promise is 'the refusal names the missing key', the refusal has to be printed where the missing key is, with the other values still in the form.

In this environment Node's fetch fails TLS with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE against every https host (corp CA in the trust store, not in Node's bundle). `node --use-system-ca <script>` fixes it, and NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca fixes the vercel CLI. gcloud's python shows the same thing as InsecureRequestWarning and `disable_ssl_validation = True` is already set in its config. A probe reporting 'fetch failed' here is an environment fact, not a finding -- and a probe that exits 2 on unreadable input is what stops that being mistaken for a pass.

A probe that reads the base URL from the ENVIRONMENT can be silently pointed at the wrong system by a leftover export. This lane's first stored 'local' run was not local: a stale SMART_FILES_BASE_URL aimed it at the production service, where its local token was correctly unknown, so it failed 401 on its first check and the artifact's own header still claimed 'local server + throwaway Postgres'. Nothing was written and no verdict rested on it, but only because the probe PRINTS its base URL as its first line. Put the effective target on line one of every probe, and read line one before reading the verdict -- the header a human typed is not evidence, the line the probe printed is.

The same probe run twice with the same run tag is not a second opinion, it is a second write. Pass 2 initially reused pass 1's tag: the probe re-uploaded its own fixtures, the same docSlug came back at v4 instead of v2, and the re-uploaded scan fixture recorded a FRESH reason, silently undoing the nulling that the legacy leg exists to test. Eight FAILs, none of them the product's. Any 'run it again to confirm' step must be a fresh identity (new tag, new room) unless the whole point is to hit the same rows.

A Vercel project with no git connection looks identical to a git-connected one from the URL: smart-files-app's production deploy was 15 days old while merges landed daily. `vercel project ls` shows the last update; check it before assuming a merge ships the UI.
DEAD_END: Trying to verify a canary with a health check or a bare curl. Both the old and the new revision answer 200 on the same URL; the tag URL is indistinguishable from production until the probe asks for a field only the new code emits.

Deploying `--source .` from the branch that carries the deploy probe itself: the probe is not in the merge commit, so the tree you want to verify and the tree you want to deploy are different. Detach at the merge SHA to deploy, then check the probe's branch back out to run it. (Cost: one failed run of 'Cannot find module'.)

leave_behind: The design's three named reasons are now a closed set in a column with a CHECK constraint, and the read path has five states including reason-not-recorded. Anything added later that needs to know WHY a document is unsearchable must read that column; inferring from content_type is the defect this row exists to prevent and it is now visible on the surface as '? Reason not recorded' on 29 production rows.

scripts/write_surface_check.mjs and scripts/g155_served_surface_check.mjs are two instruments over one vocabulary (web/design-vocabulary.json). Changing copy means running BOTH: the file check sees the repo, the served check sees the deploy, and they currently disagree only when the deploy is stale.

scripts/g155_tag_verify.mjs is the deploy-time probe for this service: it proves a revision by the fields it emits, writes nothing, and is the cheapest way to answer 'is the canary actually the new code' for any future smart-files deploy.
Production rows written before 2026-09-18T01:31Z have no recorded reason and will show 'Reason not recorded' forever unless someone re-extracts them. That is deliberate; do not 'fix' it by inferring.
The QA UI deploys by hand (vercel --prod from web/, project smart-files-app, root directory `.`), NOT by merging. A merge to main changes the API and leaves the UI exactly where it was.

Traffic on smart-files stays PINNED BY REVISION NAME with four tags now (g106-read-scope, g107-provenance, search-wave, g155-search-reason). A future `gcloud run deploy` without --no-traffic --tag will no-op and report the old revision as serving. Read traffic by JSON field name.
